overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely approve its May 6, 2024 minutes, and the violation was intentional, but no civil penalty was imposed; the unreviewed recording-announcement allegation was not addressed.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to timely approve its May 6, 2024 meeting minutes; the Board approved them July 15, 71 days later, after edits.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we do not find good cause for the Board’s delay in its approval of the minutes of the May 6 meeting, and we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to approve the minutes in a timely manner.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board Chair did not announce at the May 6, 2024 meeting that the meeting was being recorded.
allegations.key_passage: Mr. Higgins did not request further review of this allegation and we, therefore, do not review it.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
All Board members must attend a webinar training on the Open Meeting Law conducted by the Attorney General's office within 90 days.
The Board must certify to the Attorney General's office within 95 days that each member completed the webinar training.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements and caution the Board that a future finding of an intentional violation of the Open Meeting Law may result in a civil penalty of up to $1,000 per violation.
